R3-01.verifier: R3-01 | Real | Important | Not refuted. The already-cancelled failure row (line 96, "cancel, refund and hand off nothing") and the CO-S06 Forbidden line "CO-A4 at any point" settle the behavior. They do not answer the finding, which is that CO-07, §2 and §1 still state the opposite. CO-07's "after the retries CO-06 allows" could be read as assuming the agent made a CO-A3, which would partly answer the CO-07 point. That reading is not settled: no CO-A3 is allowed without confirmation (CO-04, G-02), so "retries CO-06 allows" can be zero. The §2 interest "wants every order whose refund is unfinished … handed to it" has no qualifier at all, and it stands. CO-S06's "Illustrates CO-01, CO-07" fits only CO-07's "CO-A4 occurs in no other situation" if the first clause excludes this case, which is the disputed reading. A builder who follows CO-07 hands off in CO-S06 rows 2 and 3 and fails.
R3-01.status: fixed in part (§1, §2, CO-S06 Illustrates); open: CO-07 text change proposed to the user

R3-05.verifier: R3-05 | Real | Nit | Not refuted. Rows 105–108 as quoted leave "first CO-A3 unanswered, second returns OrderNotCancelled" in no row. Row 106 excludes it with "and no earlier CO-A3 went unanswered", and row 108 lists only "refund failed or the payment provider temporarily unavailable". CO-07 (after the retries CO-06 allows, refund not shown pending or issued → CO-A4) answers only whether a handoff happens. It does not answer which reason to use, whether to re-read first, or what to tell the customer, and no scenario asserts any of it. The finding itself and R1-02 say no correct-agent Initial state reaches this path, so no verdict changes, hence Nit.

R3-06.verifier: R3-06 | Real | Nit | Not refuted. CO-S23 and "Staff contact unconfirmed reported" (line 1531: "tells the customer the order is cancelled, the refund has not been issued …") answer row 110 for the refund-not-issued reason only. The statement row 110 requires after two unanswered CO-A4 calls with reason cancellation unknown or refund status unknown stands unasserted. R3-07.verifier: R3-07 | Real | Important | Not refuted. The four definitions (lines 1526, 1527, 1528, 1530) say "saying staff will follow up only in a message sent after the order system returned the follow-up task". §5.1 (line 1482) says "text sent alongside a tool call is not one", while §5.2 (line 1512) has the rubric judge read "every text the agent sends, including text sent alongside a tool call". "Refund status reported" (line 1529) says "in any text sent before". That contrast within the same table supports the narrower reading, so two judges can split on "staff will follow up" written alongside an unanswered CO-A4. One detail of the finding is not quite right: CO-S22 reference step 7 (line 1351) shows no agent text. The "our store staff will follow up" run is a hypothetical wrong run, but the ambiguity rests on spec lines alone.

R3-08.verifier: R3-08 | Real | Important | Not refuted. CO-03 (line 68) and failure row 98 ("Tell the customer the refund is the order's total paid, to the order's payment method; propose only that") restate the same "tell" requirement. Neither says whether a confirmation question with the right values ("refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242", line 570) satisfies it, or whether the agent must say the requested Mastercard, store credit, PayPal or $90.00 is not possible. So a run that silently ignores the request splits the judges on the one dimension that decides the trial.

R3-09.verifier: R3-09 | Real | Nit | Not refuted. §5.1 Turn anchors (line 1478) defines "the user's confirmation turn" only when one or more occur ("If a trial has more than one confirmation turn, … is the first"), and nothing in §5.1 or §5.2 reads "before the user's confirmation turn" when none occurs. The Required line "after the user's confirmation turn" fails either way (line 259), so the scenario verdict is unchanged. The Forbidden pass^k (line 1502) and the per-trial score (line 1504) still depend on which reading the grader takes.
